areas.area_name: Sand removal, settling & washing (clarification and CCD residue washing)
areas.purpose: Separate the coarse sand and the fine residue (red mud) from the digested slurry. Deliver a clear pregnant (green) liquor to security filtration (A10). Recover soluble soda and dissolved alumina from the residue by counter-current decantation (CCD) washing before the residue is filtered (A09). Provide the area spill-recovery system and the refinery process-spill (emergency) catchment pond.
areas.process_description:
1) FEED: Digested slurry leaves the atmospheric blow-off tank of digestion (A07) at about 103-108 degC, close to its boiling point. It is supersaturated in alumina (A/C about 0.70-0.74) and carries about 95-110 g/L residue solids (about 285 t/h dry residue in about 2,750-2,950 m3/h liquor). The 08-PP-001 cyclone feed pumps are the ONLY pumping step between the A07 blow-off tank and the settlers. The separate A07 blow-off pump to the dilution tank is deleted, and the sand cyclones sit upstream of the settler feed (dilution) tank. A08 must be fast: from the digester to the end of security filtration the liquor is metastable. Gibbsite can autoprecipitate in settlers, tanks and launders, which loses product and builds scale, so residence time is kept short and temperature high.
2) SAND REMOVAL: The cyclone feed pumps send the slurry to two clusters of hydrocyclones that cut at about 100-150 um. Underflow (sand: quartz, coarse goethite/hematite and laterite gravel) drops to a 3-stage counter-current screw-classifier train and is washed with hot wash water. Washed sand is dewatered on a vibrating screen and conveyed to a stockpile for RSA drainage layers and roads. Cyclone overflow (fine residue plus liquor) flows to the settler feed tank. Sand content depends strongly on the ore. The DESIGN ORE is India East Coast (khondalite) gibbsitic bauxite, which is low in quartz (total SiO2 about 2-5%), so sand is about 3-8% of residue, about 9-23 t/h. The circuit is sized for a 45 t/h maximum to absorb ore variability. Darling Range ore gives roughly 40-50% of residue as quartz-rich sand and would need a sand circuit about 5-10 times larger, with multiple classifier trains. With East Coast ore there is too little sand for embankment construction, so RSA embankments use compacted residue and borrow (see A09).
3) DILUTION AND FLOCCULATION: First-washer (W1) overflow, the weak liquor at about 130-170 g/L C as Na2CO3, dilutes the cyclone overflow in the settler feed tank. This lowers viscosity and sets pregnant-liquor C (target about 240-255 g/L as Na2CO3) and A/C (0.68-0.72). Flocculant is added in stages. Hydroxamate-modified polyacrylamide goes in first, for overflow clarity: it captures fine iron and titanium minerals and DSP. High-MW sodium polyacrylate follows for settling rate. Both are dosed into the feed pipe and feedwell.
4) SETTLING (clarification): High-rate settlers (decanters) separate residue from liquor. Overflow is pregnant (green) liquor at about 10-50 mg/L suspended solids, about 100-105 degC, going to security filtration (A10). Underflow at about 30-40 wt% solids is pumped to the Washer 1 feedwell.
5) CCD WASHING: Six washer stages operate in series and a 7th is installed for descaling rotation. Mud moves forward (W1 to W6) by underflow pumping. Wash liquor moves backward. Hot wash water (RSA return water, process condensate and press filtrate, about 500-650 m3/h) enters W6. Each washer's overflow joins the feed of the washer before it, and W1 overflow returns to the settler feed tank. A side-stream of W1/W2 overflow (about 500 m3/h) goes to causticisation (A19) and returns with carbonate converted to caustic. Soluble Na2O and Al2O3 concentrations fall stage by stage (ideal-mixing model). Final underflow leaves W6 at 45-55 wt% solids with residual liquor of about 3-8 g/L total soda as Na2CO3 and is pumped to residue filtration (A09).
6) CHEMISTRY in this area: (a) Supersaturated pregnant liquor can revert, Al(OH)4- -> Al(OH)3 + OH-. Hot liquor and short residence prevent this. (b) Desilication product (DSP, sodalite type Na8[Al6Si6O24]X2 with X = 2OH-, CO3 2-, SO4 2- or Cl-) has largely formed in pre-desilication and digestion and leaves with the mud. It is the main CHEMICAL soda loss: about 0.69 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2 (sodalite stoichiometry), about 37 kg Na2O/t alumina at 2% reactive silica. Washing cannot recover it. (c) Washing recovers only SOLUBLE soda carried in the liquor that wets the mud. (d) In the later washers, where liquor is weaker and cooler, some gibbsite can precipitate (soluble alumina loss), and calcium carbonate and oxalate scale can form. Washer temperature control and rotation of the spare washer manage this.
7) WATER BALANCE: Net water added in A08 is wash water minus W6 underflow liquor, about 550 - 280 = about 270 t/h. All of it ends up in the liquor circuit and must be removed by evaporation (A18). The wash ratio therefore trades soda recovery against evaporator steam. This is a key point for trainees. Underflow density is the stronger lever: a denser underflow improves washing without adding water.
8) SPILL CONTAINMENT: Each thickener and pump bay is bunded and drains to area sumps (08-PP-031). The sumps return strong spills to the settler feed or W1 and dilute spills to the wash water tank. A refinery process-spill catchment pond (08-PD-001) receives a full thickener inventory after loss of containment, overflow from bunds in a design storm, and drain-downs that the spare thickener cannot take.
9) HIGH-TEMPERATURE (boehmitic) plants differ: digestion runs at 240-260 degC, there is typically more DSP and cancrinite, slurry is cooled through more flash stages, and settler feed liquor is often more concentrated. Settling and CCD principles are the same.

streams.name: Digested (blow-off) slurry to sand cyclones
streams.flow: About 2,750-2,950 m3/h liquor + about 285 t/h dry residue incl. sand (design 310 t/h); about 3,000-3,150 m3/h slurry
streams.pressure: Atmospheric at tank; about 2.5-3.5 bar g at pump discharge, 0.8-1.5 bar g at cyclone manifold
streams.composition: C about 255-285 g/L as Na2CO3 (after flash concentration, before dilution), A/C about 0.70-0.74, residue solids about 95-110 g/L, slurry SG about 1.40
streams.basis: Engineering estimate from 241 t/h alumina, residue 1.18 t/t (plant-wide basis), A06/A07 drafts for liquor

streams.name: Sand cyclone underflow
streams.flow: Normal about 9-23 t/h dry sand (3-8% of residue); design maximum 45 t/h; at about 50-65 wt% solids
streams.composition: Quartz, coarse goethite/hematite/laterite, +100-150 um, plus entrained fines and liquor
streams.basis: Expert review (India East Coast khondalite ore, low quartz); engineering estimate

streams.name: Washed sand to stockpile
streams.from_to: 08-SC-001 -> 08-CV-001 -> sand stockpile -> A09 RSA (drainage layers, roads)
streams.flow: About 9-23 t/h dry (about 0.07-0.19 Mt/yr), 85-90 wt% solids
streams.composition: Target residual soluble soda about 1-3 kg Na2O/t sand
streams.basis: Engineering estimate

streams.name: Settler feed (diluted slurry)
streams.flow: About 3,450-3,700 m3/h liquor + about 265-290 t/h fine residue (design about 300 t/h)
streams.composition: C about 240-255 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C about 0.68-0.72, solids about 75-85 g/L
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; mass balance with W1 overflow about 600-800 m3/h

streams.name: Settler overflow = pregnant (green) liquor
streams.composition: C 240-255 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C 0.68-0.72, suspended solids about 10-50 mg/L (up to about 100 mg/L in upsets)
streams.basis: 241 t/h / about 80 g/L yield (plant-wide basis); solids range engineering estimate from hydroxamate practice

streams.name: Settler underflow
streams.flow: About 265-300 t/h dry solids at 30-40 wt%, about 600-800 m3/h total (about 300-400 m3/h per operating settler)
streams.pressure: About 2-4 bar g at pump discharge
streams.composition: Red mud + pregnant liquor (about 400-450 m3/h liquor)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate

streams.name: Wash water to last washer
streams.from_to: 08-TK-021 (RSA return water + process condensate + A09 filtrate) -> 08-HX-001 -> W6 feedwell
streams.flow: About 500-650 m3/h (design 550; about 1.7-2.3 m3/t dry residue)
streams.composition: Total soda about 1-10 g/L as Na2CO3, pH 12-13
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; consistent with A18 water balance (CCD wash about 550 t/h)

streams.name: First washer overflow (weak liquor) to dilution
streams.from_to: W1 overflow tank -> 08-PP-021 -> 08-TK-001; side-stream about 500 m3/h W1/W2 overflow to A19 causticisation and return
streams.flow: About 600-800 m3/h
streams.composition: C about 130-170 g/L as Na2CO3 (W1), about 100-130 g/L (W2); A/C about 0.6-0.7; carbonate 20-30 g/L
streams.basis: Aligned with liquor-domain plant-wide numbers (A19/A20); engineering estimate

streams.name: Final washer underflow to residue filtration
streams.flow: About 285 t/h dry solids (design 310) at 45-55 wt%, about 370-450 m3/h
streams.composition: Liquor about 3-8 g/L total soda as Na2CO3 (about 280 m3/h liquor)
streams.basis: IAI BR Guidance 2015 (CCD underflow >40%, about 50% practical, 48-55% advanced thickeners); soda value engineering estimate

streams.name: Flocculant solutions
streams.flow: Settler about 100-300 g/t polyacrylate + 20-100 g/t hydroxamate; washers about 30-100 g/t each (dry polymer basis), diluted to 0.02-0.1%
streams.composition: High-MW sodium polyacrylate; hydroxamated polyacrylamide (settlers only)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate, vendor dependent

streams.name: Spill recovery return
streams.from_to: 08-PD-001 / area sumps -> 08-PP-041 / 08-PP-031 -> settler feed, W1 or 08-TK-021 (depending on strength)
streams.flow: Intermittent, 0-500 m3/h
streams.composition: Liquor/slurry spills, contaminated stormwater, washdown
streams.basis: Engineering estimate

equipment.name: Sand cyclone feed pumps (blow-off slurry pumps)
equipment.function: Pump hot digested slurry from the A07 blow-off tank to the sand cyclone clusters at the required manifold pressure. These are the single pumping step between digestion and clarification.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal heavy-duty centrifugal slurry pump, hard-metal (high-chrome) wet end, overhung, direct-coupled or overhead V-belt drive, VSD (Weir Warman AH/MC or equivalent class)
equipment.why_this_type: Large-volume abrasive slurry at moderate head. Hard metal withstands quartz and laterite gravel, and hot caustic at about 105 degC rules out natural rubber linings.
key_dimensions: Each about 1,500-1,700 m3/h at about 25-35 m head (engineering estimate)
Suction about 500-600 mm, discharge about 400-450 mm
Impeller dia about 1.1-1.4 m; pump + baseplate + motor footprint about 6 m x 2.5 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (3,000-3,150 m3/h total over 2 pumps)
engineering estimate (manifold 0.8-1.5 bar + static about 15-20 m + losses)
engineering estimate (rho g Q H / eta at eta about 0.70); corrected down from draft 450-750 kW

equipment.working_principle: A rotating closed impeller with thick vanes gives the slurry kinetic energy, and the volute converts it to pressure. Wear parts (impeller, throatbush, frame-plate liner, volute liner) are high-chrome white iron of about 27% Cr, which resists quartz abrasion. The slurry is at its boiling point, so the available NPSH is essentially the static head between the blow-off tank level and the pump suction, minus friction. The pumps therefore sit at the lowest elevation, close below the tank, with a short, large-bore suction. The VSD holds cyclone manifold pressure constant as feed density and the number of open cyclones change. Gland sealing uses a double mechanical seal or a flushed packing with condensate, and seal water is minimised to limit dilution.
details_to_model: Overhung pump with split, heavily bolted outer casing halves; large axial suction and tangential discharge pointing up
Bearing cartridge on pedestal with impeller-clearance adjusting screws at the rear
Direct-coupled motor (about 2 m long) with coupling guard, or overhead motor on a mounting frame with V-belt guard

Suction spool with knife-gate isolation valve (actuated), drain valve to bunded trench and flush connection; discharge with actuated knife-gate or pinch valve, diaphragm-sealed pressure gauge and transmitter
Seal-water panel with flow indicator and needle valve
Concrete plinth with drain trench in a bunded pump bay; safety shower/eyewash within 10 s
Insulated suction and discharge pipe (aluminium cladding), personnel-protection cages
Lifting lugs on casing halves; monorail with hoist above the pump bay for liner change
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry near boiling: flashes on loss of containment, severe combined caustic and thermal burns; full face shield and caustic-resistant PPE
Gland or flange spray: flange guards/spray shields
Before liner change: double block and drain, LOTO, confirm cooled and depressurised
Water hammer on pump trip with a long discharge line; discharge valve closing sequence
Radiometric density gauge on discharge (if fitted): plant radiation safety plan
sources: Engineering estimate based on typical Bayer blow-off pump practice
IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015) for circuit context
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron (about 27% Cr) wet end; ductile iron or carbon steel outer casing; hard-coated shaft sleeve
equipment.drive_and_power: LV/MV induction motor 315-450 kW with VSD
instrumentation_and_control: VSD speed control on cyclone manifold pressure
Blow-off tank level interlock (low-level trip, NPSH protection)
common_problems: Cavitation from low NPSH or flashing
Throatbush and impeller wear by gravel and sand
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never run against a closed discharge in hot slurry: it flashes within seconds
Keep blow-off tank level above the NPSH minimum
Flush the line with dilute liquor before a planned stop to avoid sanding
equipment.alternatives: Vertical cantilever pumps from a sump (smaller plants)

equipment.name: Sand cyclone clusters
equipment.function: Classify coarse sand (+100-150 um) out of the digested slurry ahead of the settlers, protecting settler rakes, underflow pumps and lines, and producing washed sand.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 clusters, each with about 5-6 cyclones in service
equipment.qty_standby: 2-3 spare positions per cluster (isolated by knife gate)
equipment.type_selected: Radial-manifold cluster of 500-660 mm hydrocyclones, ceramic- or high-chrome-lined (Weir Cavex / FLSmidth Krebs gMAX class)
equipment.why_this_type: Compact, no moving parts, sharp enough cut at 100-150 um, and individual cyclones can be exchanged online. With low-sand East Coast ore they mainly protect downstream equipment from gravel and coarse laterite.
key_dimensions: Cyclone body ID about 500-660 mm, overall cyclone height about 3-4 m (engineering estimate)
Cluster manifold dia about 3-4 m, 8 positions; cluster overall height about 6-7 m
Inlet about 250 x 125 mm; vortex finder about 200-250 mm; apex about 100-150 mm

operating_parameters.basis: expert review; 3-8% of residue for India East Coast ore

equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters tangentially and forms a vortex. Centrifugal force throws coarse, dense particles to the wall, where they spiral down and leave through the apex as underflow. Fine mud and most of the liquor reverse into the inner upward vortex and leave through the vortex finder as overflow. Cyclone diameter, manifold pressure, vortex-finder and apex sizes, and slurry viscosity set the cut size. Hot, low-viscosity liquor sharpens it. Operators adjust the number of open cyclones to hold manifold pressure as flow changes. A 'roping' apex discharge indicates overload.
details_to_model: Circular distributor (manifold) with central bottom feed and 8 radial knife-gate valves, each feeding one cyclone (inclined or vertical)
Each cyclone: cylindrical inlet head with tangential inlet, 2-3 flanged cone segments, apex/spigot with ceramic insert, vortex finder rising to the overflow launder
Annular overflow launder collecting all vortex finders, large outlet pipe to settler feed tank 08-TK-001
Underflow launder/hopper below with hood, discharge chute to classifier 08-CL-001
Manifold pressure gauge and transmitter with diaphragm seals
Steel support structure (cluster at about +15 to +20 m) with platform at cyclone-head level, grating, handrails, toe boards, stair
Monorail with chain block for cyclone change-out
Covered launders with vapour vents
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic splash from apex discharge; underflow hood required
Working at height on cluster platform
Isolate and drain each cyclone before removal
sources: Engineering estimate; vendor sizing practice for 500-660 mm hydrocyclones
Power G., Graefe M., Klauber C., Hydrometallurgy 108 (2011) 33-45, bauxite residue sand separation and use (not retrieved this session)
Expert review finding (sand fraction by ore type)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shells with ceramic (alumina/SiC) or high-chrome wear liners; natural rubber unsuitable at 100+ degC in caustic
operating_tips_and_key_points: Open or close cyclones online to hold manifold pressure
Check underflow shape every round: umbrella spray, not rope
equipment.alternatives: Gravity sand traps/rotary sand separators (older plants); for Darling Range ore a much larger multi-train circuit

equipment.name: Sand washing screw classifiers (3-stage counter-current)
equipment.function: Wash entrained caustic liquor from the sand and dewater it, recovering soda and alumina and producing low-soda sand for RSA drainage layers and roads.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (sand can be bypassed to settler feed for short maintenance)
equipment.type_selected: Inclined twin-spiral screw classifiers, high-weir type
equipment.why_this_type: Robust and simple: classifying, washing and dewatering in one machine. Tolerates gravel and is proven in Bayer sand washing. One train is enough at 9-23 t/h normal and 45 t/h maximum.
key_dimensions: Spiral dia about 1.2-1.5 m, trough length about 9-11 m, incline about 14-18 degrees (engineering estimate)
Pool area at lower end about 10-18 m2
Each about 15-25 t operating mass
equipment.working_principle: Sand slurry enters a pool at the lower end of an inclined trough. Coarse sand settles and is carried up the incline by slowly rotating helical spirals, draining as it rises out of the pool. Fines and liquor overflow the weir at the lower end. Wash liquor flows counter-current: fresh hot wash water enters stage 3, stage 3 overflow washes stage 2, stage 2 overflow washes stage 1, and stage 1 overflow returns to the settler feed tank. Sand leaving stage 3 carries only weak liquor.
details_to_model: Long inclined steel trough with rectangular pool at lower end, adjustable overflow weir and launder
Two parallel helical spirals on hollow shafts with bolt-on hardened wear shoes
Upper-end drive: motor + shaft-mounted reducer with guard; lower bearing with lifting mechanism (screw jack or hydraulic) to raise spirals out of sand
Feed box at mid-pool; wash-water spray bars over the rising sand bed
Sand discharge chute at upper end onto next stage or dewatering screen
Pool covers with vapour extraction duct; walkways both sides, stairs
Trough drains and flushing connections
hazards_and_safety: Rotating spirals: interlocked covers, LOTO before entry
Confined space if trough is entered for wear-shoe replacement
sources: Engineering estimate; classical Bayer sand washing practice
equipment.materials: Carbon steel trough, PWHT of welds per owner caustic-service materials philosophy (NACE SP0403 chart); hardened wear shoes
equipment.drive_and_power: Electric motor 11-30 kW per classifier with helical-bevel reducer; hydraulic or electric lift
common_problems: Spiral overload on restart after sanding
operating_tips_and_key_points: Lift spirals before stopping with a full sand load
Keep wash water hot to keep viscosity low
equipment.alternatives: Sand-wash hydrocyclones + dewatering screen; bucket-wheel sand washers

equipment.name: Sand dewatering screen
equipment.function: Final dewatering of washed sand to a conveyable, stackable product.
equipment.type_selected: Linear-motion high-frequency dewatering screen with polyurethane panels (0.5-1.0 mm aperture)
equipment.why_this_type: Gives about 85-90 wt% solids sand for conveying.
key_dimensions: Deck about 1.5-2.0 m wide x 4.0-5.0 m long (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Twin unbalanced-mass vibrator motors produce a linear stroke. Sand forms a bed that acts as its own filter as water drains through the PU panels. The deck slopes slightly upward to the discharge to hold the bed.
details_to_model: Box-like screen body on coil or rubber springs, two exciter motors on a top cross-beam
Modular PU panels in a grid, ribbed side plates
Under-pan sloping to filtrate pipe back to classifier stage 3
Discharge lip over conveyor 08-CV-001; vented enclosure
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check panel wear and blinding every shift
equipment.alternatives: Draining stockpile on a sloped pad

equipment.name: Sand conveyor and sand stockpile
equipment.function: Convey washed sand to a bunded stockpile for truck haulage to the RSA (drainage layers, roads).
equipment.type_selected: Troughed belt conveyor (CEMA C/D idlers), 650-800 mm belt; bunded concrete stockpile pad with drainage sump
equipment.why_this_type: Low capacity, short distance.
key_dimensions: Belt width 650-800 mm, length about 50-150 m (engineering estimate)
Stockpile pad about 30 x 25 m, about 5-7 days at normal sand rate
equipment.working_principle: A troughed belt on idlers, driven by a head pulley, carries the sand. Pad drainage (weak caustic) collects in a sump and returns to the process.
details_to_model: Galvanised truss gallery with walkway, handrails and pull-wire emergency stop
Head drive (motor, gearbox) with guarding; tail pulley with take-up
Head scrapers; skirtboards at loading
Stockpile pad with push walls, drain grate and sump pump; front-end loader
hazards_and_safety: Alkaline sand (pH > 11): skin and eye irritation
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials (practice)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Monitor sand soda: it decides whether the sand is fit for RSA drainage use
equipment.alternatives: Direct truck loadout

equipment.name: Settler feed (dilution) tank
equipment.function: Combine cyclone overflow with W1 overflow, classifier overflow and A10 sluice returns, dilute to target pregnant-liquor concentration, and split the flow to the operating settlers.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated cylindrical vertical tank, fixed roof, insulated, with distributor box
equipment.why_this_type: Short-residence (3-8 min) mixing vessel that minimises time for autoprecipitation.
key_dimensions: About 8-10 m ID x 8-10 m high (engineering estimate)
Live volume about 300-500 m3
equipment.working_principle: A top-entry agitator mixes the streams uniformly. An overflow distributor box with gates splits flow equally to the operating settlers.
details_to_model: Top-entry agitator (2 pitched-blade impellers) with gearbox on roof bridge
Inlet nozzles: cyclone overflow, W1 overflow, classifier overflow, A10 sluice return, flush; outlet distributor box with 3 gates (one per settler)
Insulation with aluminium cladding, roof manway, vent, radar level
Stair tower to roof, handrails
equipment.materials: Carbon steel, PWHT welds per owner caustic-service philosophy (NACE SP0403)
instrumentation_and_control: Online caustic/alumina analyser (titrator) or density/conductivity on outlet
operating_tips_and_key_points: Control W1 overflow dilution to hold pregnant-liquor C and A/C on target
equipment.alternatives: Inline dilution in pipe/launder

equipment.name: High-rate settlers (mud decanters)
equipment.function: Separate fine residue from pregnant liquor, giving clear overflow for security filtration and thickened underflow for washing.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (rotated for descaling, about every 3-12 months; engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: High-rate thickener with deep energy-dissipating, flocculant-dilution feedwell, centre-column hydraulic rake drive, fixed insulated roof
equipment.why_this_type: Synthetic flocculants allow several times the unit-area capacity of old multi-tray settlers, cutting liquor holdup (autoprecipitation and soda inventory). A spare unit is needed because gibbsite and DSP scale accumulates.
key_dimensions: ID about 40-45 m; sidewall about 6-8 m; floor slope about 1:6 to 1:4 (engineering estimate)
Feedwell about 6-8 m dia x 3-4 m deep
Centre column about 3-4 m dia
Mud bed depth typically 1-3 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (3,000-3,300 m3/h over 2 x 40-45 m)

equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters the feedwell, where velocity is dissipated and flocculant is mixed in so fine particles aggregate into large, fast-settling flocs. Flocs settle through a hindered-settling zone into a compression bed, and clear liquor rises over the peripheral launder weirs. Slowly rotating rake arms (about 1 rev per 10-20 min) with angled blades move compacted mud to the central discharge cone and open channels for liquor to escape the bed. Hydroxamate flocculant is selective for iron-oxide fines and sets overflow clarity, while polyacrylate builds large flocs for settling rate. Bed level and rake torque are the key controls. Too high a bed raises torque and risks solids carry-over and longer liquor residence; too low a bed gives a thin underflow.
details_to_model: Large flat-bottomed cylindrical steel tank on a concrete ring wall/raft; shallow conical floor with grout fill, underflow cone at centre
Underflow tunnel or under-tank chamber with underflow pipes, knife-gate valves and pumps 08-PP-002; tunnel lighting, forced ventilation, two escape stairs
Fixed centre column carrying the rake drive on a top drive platform with hydraulic power unit and lift cylinders
Rake: 2 long + 2 short truss arms with angled blades, cone scraper, optional pickets; rake lift 600-900 mm
Access bridge from tank wall to centre platform (about 20-22 m span) with handrails, carrying feed pipe and flocculant lines
Feedwell hung from bridge/column with multiple flocculant sparge points
Peripheral internal overflow launder with V-notch weirs, outlet box to unfiltered liquor tank 10-TK-001; covered launder
Fixed conical roof on rafters with vapour vents, inspection hatches, sampling ports
Wall insulation (mineral wool about 75-100 mm + aluminium cladding)
Instruments: bed-level sonar/profiler hanging from bridge, rake torque indicator at drive, overflow turbidity, radiometric density gauge on underflow line
Zig-zag wall stair with landings, roof walkways
Scour/flush nozzles in cone; emergency drain connection to spill header/08-PD-001
Bund wall around thickener farm
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor near boiling: burns, flashing
Confined-space entry during descaling: drain, cool, ventilate, gas test, LOTO on rake drive; entrapment in soft mud
Rake overload or collapse: torque trip, lift on high torque
Underflow tunnel: confined/low-lying space, flooding risk, possible poor atmosphere
Vapour plumes reduce visibility on roof
Radiometric gauges: plant radiation safety plan and source register
sources: IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015): high-rate decanters, super thickeners, CCD practice
Engineering estimate for dimensions and loadings
Hydroxamate flocculant practice: Cytec/Solvay HX literature and TMS Light Metals papers (not retrieved this session)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A516-70 or equivalent); welds PWHT per owner caustic-service philosophy (NACE SP0403); no internal lining; carbon steel rake
equipment.drive_and_power: Hydraulic planetary rake drive, about 15-30 kW HPU; rated torque about 1.5-3.5 MNm (engineering estimate)
instrumentation_and_control: Bed level (sonar or profiler) and bed mass (pressure)
Underflow density (radiometric) and flow (magflow) controlling underflow pump speed
Flocculant ratio control on feed solids
common_problems: Gibbsite autoprecipitation and DSP scale on walls, launders and rakes
Poor overflow clarity from wrong flocculant dose, temperature drop or sand carry-over
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the bed low enough to limit liquor residence but high enough for underflow density
Respond to rising torque by raising the rake and increasing underflow
Trim hydroxamate dose on overflow clarity: it sets security filter load directly
Plan descale rotation; keep the standby settler full of hot liquor if possible
equipment.alternatives: Conventional low-rate or multi-tray settlers; deep-cone settlers

equipment.name: Settler underflow pumps
equipment.function: Withdraw thickened mud from each settler and pump it to the Washer 1 feedwell.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 per settler (installed spare); 6 installed in total
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pumps, hard-metal wet end, VSD
equipment.why_this_type: Moderate-density (30-40 wt%) hot slurry; VSD gives density control.
key_dimensions: Each about 300-450 m3/h at 25-40 m head; 250/200 mm class (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Centrifugal slurry pump. Speed is cascaded from underflow density and bed level.
details_to_model: Located in underflow tunnel/under-tank chamber
Suction from cone with 2 knife-gate valves, flush connection, density gauge on discharge

areas.purpose: Dewater washed residue to a high-solids filter cake for dry stacking, with cake washing to minimise soluble soda and alkalinity. Transport the cake to a lined, engineered residue storage area (dry stack) managed to GISTM/ICOLD/ANCOLD practice, and return alkaline water to the refinery so no untreated discharge leaves site.
areas.process_description:
1) FILTER FEED: W6 underflow (about 285 t/h dry normal, 310 t/h design, at 45-55 wt% solids and 3-8 g/L soda as Na2CO3) goes to two agitated filter feed tanks, one per press building, with about 10-14 h combined buffer.
2) PRESS FILTRATION: Recessed-chamber membrane filter presses (2.0 x 2.0 m plates, about 1,000 m2 each) are filled by dedicated feed pumps at rising pressure up to about 7-10 bar g (engineering estimate). The cake is optionally washed with hot water to displace residual liquor, membrane-squeezed at about 15-16 bar g and briefly air-blown. Plates are then opened and the cake drops onto conveyors below. A complete cycle (close, fill, squeeze, wash, blow, open, plate shift and discharge of about 140 chambers, periodic cloth wash) takes about 60-90 min. Each press holds about 20 m3 of cake per cycle (1,000 m2 / 2 x 0.04 m), about 28-30 t dry, so it delivers about 20-25 t/h dry. 14 operating presses + 2 standby (16 installed, in two buildings of 8) cover the 310 t/h design. Cake reaches about 70-78 wt% solids (22-30% moisture). Published references: press cake >70% solids (IAI 2015); Alunorte about 22% moisture; CHALCO Zhongzhou 27-30% moisture with 600-800 m2 presses; typical 23-27% moisture (Wikipedia, Red mud). Vendor pilot press tests on project residue are required before final sizing.
3) FILTRATE: Filtrate (low soda) is collected and returned as wash water to the CCD (08-TK-021). This closes the soda loop.
4) CAKE HANDLING: Under-press belts collect each batch drop and transfer it via collector conveyors to a truck loadout bin. Articulated dump trucks haul it 2-5 km (engineering estimate) to the active RSA cell. An overland conveyor with mobile stacker is the main alternative at about 3.2 Mt/yr wet.
5) DRY STACKING AND MUD FARMING: Cake is spread in thin layers of about 0.3-0.5 m by dozer, turned and conditioned by amphirol and/or harrow to speed drying and atmospheric carbonation, then compacted. Thin-layer stacking uses 0.3-0.5 m layers dried to about 70% solids before the next layer; EGA Al Taweelah places residue in 300 mm layers with 5 m lifts (IAI 2015).
6) NEUTRALISATION / ALKALINITY REDUCTION, base case: (a) cake washing in the press; (b) atmospheric carbonation of the stack surface during farming, CO2 + 2OH- -> CO3 2- + H2O and Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O -> 2NaHCO3, with tricalcium aluminate and other alkaline solids buffering pH so it falls only gradually; (c) all lake water and underdrainage returned to the refinery. Option with a CO2 source (space provided): CO2 carbonation of filter feed (Alcoa Kwinana concept; reported pH reduction from about 13 to about 10.5 using CO2 from a neighbouring ammonia plant, not retrieved this session). Option for a coastal site: seawater neutralisation of residue or lake water. Mg2+ and Ca2+ in seawater precipitate the hydroxide and carbonate alkalinity as brucite, hydrotalcite and calcite, giving pH about 8-8.5 (IAI 2015; QAL supernatant <8.5 pH, <30 mg/L solids, <5 mg/L Al, 50 m diffuser).
7) RSA: The stack is built in cells on a composite-lined base (HDPE geomembrane over compacted low-permeability clay), with a drainage blanket and slotted pipes to sumps, perimeter starter embankments of compacted borrow, later raises of compacted residue, upstream or centreline raises in 2-5 m lifts, a decant/stormwater pond (residue lake), seepage interception and groundwater bores. With the low-sand East Coast design ore (about 0.07-0.19 Mt/yr sand), washed sand covers only part of the drainage blanket, so imported gravel/sand and compacted residue are needed for drains and embankments. Governance follows the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM, 2020: 6 topic areas, 15 principles, 77 requirements), ICOLD bulletins on tailings dams and ANCOLD Guidelines on Tailings Dams. Consequence classification uses GISTM Annex 2.
8) Wet disposal (lagooning at 18-22% solids, IAI 2015), historically common in India and worldwide, is NOT selected because of footprint, seepage and dam-break risk (Ajka 2010: about 1 Mm3 released, 10 deaths).

areas.purpose: Remove the last fine residue particles (iron and titanium minerals, DSP) from the settler overflow so that the pregnant liquor sent to heat interchange and precipitation is practically solids-free. This protects alumina purity (Fe2O3, SiO2 and TiO2 in smelter-grade alumina) and prevents fouling of the heat interchangers.
areas.process_description:
1) Settler overflow (green liquor, about 10-50 mg/L solids, about 100-105 degC) flows by gravity to the unfiltered liquor tank. Security filter feed pumps deliver it to a bank of horizontal pressure leaf filters (Kelly type).
2) FILTER AID: Tricalcium aluminate (TCA, Ca3[Al(OH)6]2, also written 3CaO.Al2O3.6H2O) is made on site by reacting slaked lime with aluminate liquor: 3Ca(OH)2 + 2Al(OH)4- -> Ca3[Al(OH)6]2 + 2OH-. TCA forms hard hexagonal/cubic crystals that make a porous, incompressible precoat and cake.
3) CYCLE (engineering estimate): (a) fill the filter with liquor; (b) precoat by recirculating TCA slurry until the filtrate is clear (about 10-20 min); (c) filter with TCA body feed until differential pressure reaches about 3-4 bar or the time limit (about 4-12 h); (d) drain the heel back to the feed tank; (e) sluice cake off the leaves with dilute liquor sprays while the sluice header oscillates; (f) send the sluiced slurry to the cake tank and pump it back to the settler feed tank or Washer 1, so residue and TCA leave via the CCD; (g) return to service. Leaves are periodically pulled and cloths descaled or replaced.
4) Filtrate turbidity is monitored on each filter. Filtered pregnant liquor goes to the filtered liquor tank and then to heat interchange (A11) at 98-104 degC.
5) Target filtrate solids < about 5-10 mg/L, typically < 5 mg/L (engineering estimate). The trade-off is TCA dosing: lime consumption plus a small alumina loss to TCA.

equipment.working_principle: Liquor fills the shell around the leaves. Staggered cycles across many filters give continuous overall flow.

decisions.finding: [process, minor] Sand fraction of 10-15% of residue matches neither reference ore; for India East Coast design ore set 3-8% (about 10-25 t/h) with 45 t/h design maximum; note Darling Range needs a circuit 5-10x larger
decisions.reason: Khondalite East Coast bauxite has low quartz (total SiO2 about 2-5%), while Darling Range residue is roughly half sand. Sand set to 3-8% of the revised 285 t/h residue (9-23 t/h), 45 t/h design maximum kept, classifier/screen/conveyor downsized, and the Darling Range note added. Added the consequence that washed sand cannot supply RSA embankments, so borrow and compacted residue are used.

decisions.finding: [mechanical, major] Filter press cycle of 20-40 min and 40-55 t/h per press is optimistic; real cycle is 60-120 min, about 20-25 t/h per 1,000 m2 press; need about 12-14 + 2 presses (or about 10 + 2 larger) and resized building and ancillaries
decisions.reason: Verified by calculation: 1,000 m2 x 0.04 m / 2 = 20 m3 cake; at about 1.5 t/m3 dry bulk density (red mud solids SG about 3.1, 74 wt% solids) about 28-30 t dry per cycle. At 60-90 min that is 20-28 t/h. With the corrected 310 t/h design residue this needs 14 operating + 2 standby (16 installed, two buildings of 8). Feed tanks (2), feed pumps (one per press), squeeze water, cloth wash, compressed air (4+1), conveyors, cranes and building size were all resized. Vendor pilot tests flagged.

Added 08-PD-001 (about 40,000-80,000 m3, double-lined with leak detection, return pumps 08-PP-041) and extended 08-PP-031 with a spill-recovery header that routes spills by strength.

open_questions: Research limitation: WebSearch returned HTTP 403 again in this session. Only Wikipedia 'Red mud' was re-fetched (it confirms 1-1.5 t/t residue with a global average of 1.23, cake moisture of 23-27%, pH 10-13, and high-density slurry at 48-55% solids). Press cycle times, thickener loadings, Kelly filter flux and the NACE SP0403 thresholds still need SME or vendor confirmation.

Filter press sizing (14 + 2 at about 1,000 m2, 60-90 min) must be confirmed by vendor pilot press tests on project residue. Choosing 2.5 x 2.5 m plates (about 10 + 2) would change building length and conveyor layout.
Residue rate: A06 (400-430 t/h) must be corrected to the agreed 285 t/h normal / 310 t/h design, and A20 aligned.
A07 owner to delete the blow-off pump to the dilution tank and confirm blow-off tank elevation and level for 08-PP-001 NPSH.

TCA lime: this area estimates about 1-2 kg CaO/t alumina from TCA stoichiometry and filter loading, while the liquor domain budgets about 6 kg/t. Reconcile with A19; this is minor against the about 40 kg/t plant total.
Process-spill pond 08-PD-001 size depends on site hydrology (design storm, process catchment area) and on whether adjacent areas (A06/A07/A10/A19) also drain to it. Confirm a single plant-wide owner.
Site location (coastal or inland) decides whether seawater neutralisation is an option. Base case: inland dry stack with atmospheric carbonation and a CO2 carbonation provision.
Climate (monsoon or Mediterranean) drives RSA water balance, pond size and wet-season trafficability; a hydrological basis is needed.
With low-sand East Coast ore, RSA drainage blankets and starter embankments need imported granular material and borrow. A borrow source and quantity study is required.
Residue transport: ADT haul (base) vs overland conveyor and stacker at about 3.2 Mt/yr wet; decide with RSA location.
Applicable national regulations (e.g. India CPCB red mud guidelines, or WA DMIRS/ANCOLD) and the GISTM consequence classification need to be defined.
Security filtration: Kelly leaf filters selected; Alcoa-style sand filters or candle filters could be preferred. Confirm against the product Fe2O3 specification (<=0.02%).
Residue reuse (cement, iron recovery, road base) could reduce RSA volume but is not in the base design.
